==Problem==
How many perfect cubes lie between <math>2^8+1</math> and <math>2^{18}+1</math>, inclusive?

<math>\textbf{(A) }4\qquad\textbf{(B) }9\qquad\textbf{(C) }10\qquad\textbf{(D) }57\qquad \textbf{(E) }58</math>

==Solution 1 (Brute force)==
First, <imath>2^8+1=257</imath>. Then, <imath>2^{18}+1=262145</imath>. Now, we can see how many perfect cubes are between these two parameters. By guessing and checking, we find that it starts from <imath>7</imath> and ends with <imath>64</imath>. Now, by counting how many numbers are between these, we find the answer to be <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E) }58}</imath>.
(You can do this, but it will still take a few minutes. Try to do something else)

==Solution 2 (If you do not notice that <imath>2^{18}=(2^6)^3=64^3</imath>)==

There is not so much guessing and checking after we find that it starts from <imath>7</imath> because <imath>7^3=343</imath>, which is over <imath>2^8+1=257</imath>. We can start guessing with the 10, answer C, as it is the middle value. Adding 10 to 7 gives us 17 and <imath>17^3 = 4,913</imath>, which is a bit low. So, we move "up" to 57, answer D. Adding 57 to 7 gives us 64 and <imath>64^3 = 262,144</imath>, which is perfect for the <imath>2^{18}+1=262,145</imath>. But we are not done. Since it is inclusive, we must add 1 to this solution, which give us <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E) }58}</imath>.

==Solution 3 (Super fast!)==

We can immediately evaluate <imath>2^8+1</imath> which gives us <imath>257</imath> and the smallest perfect cube greater than that is <imath>343 = 7^3</imath>, and you also immediately notice that <imath>2^{18} = (2^6)^3 = 64^3</imath>. Now, all we have to do is count the cubes, which equals:
\begin{align}
64-7+1 &= \boxed{\textbf{(E) }58}
\end{align}

-jb2015007

==Solution 4(Bascially the same as solution 3)==
We know that <imath>2^8+1=257</imath> which is only a little higher than <imath>6^3=216</imath>. This means that the lower bound of this is <imath>7^3</imath>. <imath>2^{18}</imath> is the same thing is <imath>64^3</imath>, which must be the upper bound. This results in <imath>64-7+1= \boxed{\textbf{(E) }58}</imath>
